subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw own pace-aware Anthropic/autonomous-agent throttling in core, and should the first scope be read-only pace visibility or enforcement?
rationale: The request adds provider-specific usage semantics, persisted state, new config, status/tool output, and autonomous-agent policy that the repo treats as compatibility-sensitive product surface.

options.title: Fold Into Resource Governance
options.body: Use this issue as part of a broader rate-limit, provider-pool, and budget design before introducing a standalone agents.defaults.pace surface.

options.title: Ship Read-Only Pace First
options.body: Expose pace projection in status and session_status while leaving throttling/enforcement out until policy is settled.

options.title: Keep Core Generic
options.body: Limit core to provider usage hooks and ask for a plugin or skill implementation unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Resource Governance
recommendation.body: Use this issue as part of a broader rate-limit, provider-pool, and budget design before introducing a standalone agents.defaults.pace surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current-main history across provider-usage, status, and auth-profile usage paths.
